item.title: Re: Why is this an SCP?
item.content:encoded:
This is an SCP for the following reasons:

  • This couldn't possibly have evolved naturally (nothing in nature remotely like it)
  • Public knowledge would probably cause panic (one of these could be in your house ready to eat your baby!)

item.title: Why is this an SCP?
item.content:encoded:
This sounds like a possible weird dangerous animal that could exist. I mean, that is not enough reason to not make it an SCP… But I just don't see why the Foundation would hide this one if by existing it does not seem to cause controversy on real science etc.

Like we have sophomores existing and tons of weird animals irl. Just because this one is dangerous I can't imagine the Foundation being all worried that people got to know this weird fungi animal.

Neutral vote from me.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I was digging the concept, imagining huge, dense, quadrapedal dust-bunnies with giant mouths full of teeth, until I hit the species list. While I still like the type A, and the tactic of type D is great (should be the standard), the other variants seem ridiculous. For the most part, it just feels like slapping on added abilities with no reason besides "because". The base species seems to be a fairly successful predator, so I don't see any reason for the variant abilites to have evolved (assuming that this is a naturally occuring creature, and not some mad scientist's homebrew).

For the time being, neutral vote.
